question.problem: If the sixth term of a geometric sequence is $\frac{1}{16}$ and the common ratio is $\frac{1}{4},$ then the third term of this sequence is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The common ratio is $r=\frac{1}{4},$ so we can start writing the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we still need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}.$ We know that the $6$th term is ${a}_{6}=16,$ so we can solve for the first term as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{6-1} \\ \frac{1}{16} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{5} \\ \frac{1}{{4}^{2}} & ={a}_{1}\cdot \frac{1}{{4}^{5}} \\ \frac{{4}^{5}}{{4}^{2}} & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =64\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know the first term is ${a}_{1}=64,$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{n-1} \\  & =64\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can use this formula to compute the third term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & =64\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{3-1} \\  & ={4}^{3}\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{2} \\  & ={4}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{{4}^{2}} \\  & ={4}^{1} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the third term  is ${a}_{3}=4.$
